Our ambition is to contribute to and support a low or zero carbon emission future by off.ligaering customers and members mobility and energy solutions with a lower climate impact, while improving the ESG performance in our entire value chain. Based on the science, which proves the impending global climate crises, we have formed our climate targets. By 2035, OKQ8 Scandinavia will achieve net-zero greenhouse gas (CO2e) emissions throughout our value chain, with a near term goal in 2025 for our own operations.

OK-Q8 AB is owned by OK ekonomisk förening and Kuwait Petroleum Europe BV. OK ekonomisk förening, with 1.9 million members in Sweden, holds a 50 percent share. Kuwait Petroleum Europe BV, known by the trademark Q8, holds the remaining 50 percent share. OKQ8 Scandinavia operates an extensive network comprising more than 1.000 service stations and 10 fuel depots under OKQ8 in Sweden and Q8 in Denmark, hereafter referred to as OKQ8 and Q8 respectively. New market conditions are taking shape. As the European Union (EU) introduces legislation, such as the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), the demand for sustainable solutions from key stakeholders grows. This supports our goals of reaching net-zero emissions by 2035 along with other sustainability goals.

Market development happens during international unrest; the war in Ukraine and Sweden's recent NATO membership impacts OKQ8 Scandinavia and our role in society. As one of the largest fuel providers in the Nordics we are a key agent in securing critical infrastructure, as we contribute to Sweden and Denmark's ability to transport goods and people, to secure industrial production and ultimately supply the military with energy solutions that can protect civilians and territory. We are working closely with the Danish and Swedish state agencies to protect the physical and digital infrastructure that safeguards free movement within and across the borders in both Scandinavia and Europe.

In 2023-2024 OKQ8 and Q8 complied with the particular greenhouse gas reduction requirements in Sweden and Denmark respectively, following the EU's Fuel Quality Directive. At a national level, the Swedish Government made significant changes to the Swedish greenhouse gas reduction mandate. The greenhouse gas reduction mandate was introduced in 2018 to contribute to Sweden's national target to lower CO2e emissions from domestic transport by 70 percent by 2030. The law stipulates a certain greenhouse gas emissions reduction from diesel and gasoline through the blending of bio-based fuels. In 2023 the Swedish government decided to alter the requirement for reduced emissions for gasoline and diesel to six percent for 2024-2026. In 2023 the reduction levels were 7,8 percent for gasoline and 30,5 percent for diesel, hence a significant change in the coming years.

content_text: As the required amount of biofuel mixed in the products to achieve the emission reductions is lowered, we expect the price of the fossil fuel products we sell to decrease. The consequences of the legislative changes in Sweden will most likely result in higher CO2e emissions for us, our customers, and the transport industry in 2024. Despite the legislative changes, OKQ8 Scandinavia will maintain and achieve our climate targets: To reach net-zero by 2035 in Scope 1, 2, and 3, by continuously adjusting our plans, investments, and product mix. For example, we developed a service that enables our customers to track and lower their CO2e emissions, by replacing diesel and gasoline with alternatives such as electric charging and biofuels. We can thereby assist customers who wish to continue with decarbonization.

By sourcing responsibly, setting requirements on our suppliers, collaborating with partners who invest in decarbonization, and by proactively offering low footprint products to customers, our ambition is to move away from a fossil-based portfolio of products. By changing our product range, we reduce our CO2e emissions and thereby take action on climate change. Because 98,5 percent of our CO2e emissions stem from the fossil fuel products we procure and sell, it underlines that climate is one of the most important and material topics for OKQ8 Scandinavia to focus on. To successfully partake in mitigating and reversing climate change, we need to address multiple material topics, as ecosystems are interdependent. We have therefore set targets that also cover and address biodiversity and pollution, as well as water, energy, and waste management. Not only covering the products we offer, but also our own operations. Just as our operations and products affect the planet, so are we responsible for the wellbeing of the people and communities we connect with. Hence, we focus on how we can enable people and communities to work, collaborate, and trade with us in a safe and transparent way. Overall, our sustainability strategy is based on a comprehensive analysis and stakeholder involvement conducted in 2020-21. In 202324, we have initiated a thorough screening of our established material topics. During 2024 we plan to conduct a double materiality analysis to ensure that our sustainability KPIs and material topics are still in line with stakeholders' expectations and requirements ahead of OKQ8 Scandinavia's obligated CSRD reporting for the 2025-26 financial year. In our commitment to accelerate electrification and minimize the environmental impact of road transportation, OKQ8 Scandinavia is actively expanding our High Power Charger (HPC) network, in partnership with Skellefteå Kraft. With a focus on greater accessibility to High Power Charging, our strategy involves deploying over 1.100 charging points, delivering minimum 150 kW output for quick charging of renewable energy, at approximately 400 locations across Scandinavia by 2026. As of February 2024, we have installed 438 High Power Charging points at a total of 107 sites. Responding to the heightened demand for High Power Charging, we expanded our Q8 station on Ørestads Boulevard in January 2024, introducing four additional High Power Chargers. This solidifies Q8 Ørestads Boulevard as OKQ8 Scandinavia's largest charging station, boasting a total of 7 High Power Chargers and 14 charging points.

In partnership with shopping center and real estate company Steen & Strøm, we are collaborating to install 240 public charging points across four major shopping centersAllum and Emporia in Sweden, and Fields and Bruuns Galleri in Denmark-to improve access to public electric vehicle charging for private customers on the go.

In the autumn of 2023, the first High Power Charger for heavy vehicles opened in Halmstad as part of the joint initiative by OKQ8, Skellefteå Kraft, and Volvo Trucks. The ambition is to create Sweden's largest network of public charging stations for heavy vehicles, promoting the shift to electric road transport and enhancing flexibility for haulers and companies investing in electric heavy goods vehicles. The plan is to install a total of 41 charging stations for heavy vehicles, which will be strategically located at either Volvo Trucks or OKQ8 facilities in various places, including Sollentuna, Jönköping, and Umeå. Each location will be equipped with two to four charging points, each delivering a continuous power of 350 kW.

As of November 2023, Move About's carpools, located at more than 120 sites across 30 cities in Sweden, has become part of OKQ8. Through this, OKQ8 contributes to increased access to shared cars near where people live and work, reducing the need for individuals to own their own cars. A privately owned car remains stationary approximately 95 percent of the time. However, by sharing resources through a carpool, both businesses and individuals can save money, contribute to reduced congestion in cities, and lower CO2e emissions. The carpools will primarily consist of electric vehicles but also include hybrids for companies that prefer them. Cars can be conveniently booked and unlocked through the Move About app.

We want to support our business customers in their transition, and our Transition Model aims to offer clear insights into the environmental and economic aspects of adopting less carbon-intensive road transport options. The model assesses the potential CO2e savings and associated costs for business clients transitioning to alternative fuels or electric vehicles, by considering factors like vehicle count, fuel type and volume. - We are OKQ8 Scandinavia

Our solar energy business unit, SunDay, which supplies solar energy, charging and storage for the business sector, is experiencing continued growth. Throughout the year, SunDay has finalized four solar parks (28 MW) and is entrusted with the construction of three additional solar parks (15 MW) in Finland. This includes the nation's largest in Kalajoki-a project awarded to SunDay by the client, Solarigo. All facilities are highly efficient and built with the latest technology. In Sweden, over 4.600 solar panels have been installed for roof-top installations, providing over 2.000 kW, together with 200 charging stations with low power chargers. As an example, we successfully implemented a sizable solar power facility (180kW) and deployed a significant number of electric vehicle chargers at Kneippbyn Resort on Gotland. This initiative aligns with the resort's commitment to reduce its carbon footprint. In the next fiscal year, SunDay's objective is to start off the first turnkey solar park projects and increase the volume of other solar park projects substantially. There is also an increased market for battery solutions and SunDay has received several orders for large batteries that will be installed during 2024.

Through KP, we are one of the leading cleantech wholesalers in the Nordics. By delivering advanced products and smart services within solar energy, charging infrastructure and energy storage to hundreds of retailers, KP is contributing to the acceleration of the renewable energy transition. Over the past year, our solar panel sales amounted to an annual output of 84,5 GWh, providing electricity equivalent to the needs of 8.460 households. Additionally, KP has strategically expanded its operations in Finland, strengthening our Nordic presence and reinforcing our commitment to fostering renewable energy solutions throughout the region.

OKQ8 Scandinavia is in a strategic partnership with Neste, the world's leading producer of biodiesel (HVO100). This collaboration has established one of Sweden's most extensive networks of stations offering HVO100. NesteMY's HVO100 meets rigorous criteria, ensuring traceability throughout the entire supply chain and conducting CO2e reduction calculations for each batch. HVO100 is compatible with all engines approved for XTL, providing a means of reducing greenhouse gas emissions from internal combustion engine vehicles while awaiting the development of other technologies. Since February 2024, HVO100 is now available at 345 stations in Sweden and 10 stations in Denmark.

content_text: Throughout the year, we have introduced a new sandwich concept at Q8, featuring a diverse range of sandwiches designed to increase animal welfare and minimize the impact on the environment. Firstly, the sandwich bread is made of 100 percent organic ingredients. The salad in the sandwiches is sourced from greenhouses that utilize 95 percent less water in their production processes and all dressings used are plant-based. Furthermore, specific sandwiches within this new lineup showcase unique attributes. The Teriyaki sandwich, for instance, is entirely plantbased. In the Chicken and Bacon sandwich, the chicken has the Danish Animal Welfare Label with 2 hearts and the bacon comes from a byproduct. Certain bacon is not sold to the restaurant and retail sectors because of its physical appearance, such as uneven cuts. It's important to note that these aesthetic considerations have no bearing on its taste. Consequently, we've chosen to purchase this imperfect bacon to assist the producer in minimizing food waste. To achieve our objective of reducing CO2e emissions in our own operations and value chain, we follow the Greenhouse Gas Protocol calculation method. Our target is composed of Scope 1 and 2 targets, such as the emissions from our own operations, and a Scope 3 target covering our value chain. OKQ8 Scandinavia has set a goal to reach net-zero by 2035, meaning we will reduce our CO2e emissions by at least 90 percent in Scope 1, 2 and 3 compared to our 2020 baseline. We will compensate for the residual CO2e (max. 10 percent) emissions following the Science Based Target initiative (SBTi) method. In 2020 OKQ8 Scandinavia committed to having our climate targets approved as ScienceBased Targets. Since then, we have been waiting for SBTi to publish the methodology for the oil and gas sector, which is still pending. Meanwhile, our commitment remains. Scope 3 accounts for 99,9 percent of OKQ8 Scandinavia's CO2e emissions per 2023-2024, with fuels and oils accounting for 98,5 percent of Scope 3. In 2023 we have reduced our Scope 3 CO2e emissions by 3,2 percent, due to a decrease in sales of fuels. In 2023 the Swedish government altered the Greenhouse gas reduction mandate legislation. We expect this to result in higher CO2e emissions for us, our customers, and the whole transport industry from 2024. Despite the legislative changes, we maintain our 2035 climate target. You can read more about this on page 9.

Scope 1 encompasses CO2e emissions generated at our facilities and by our company vehicles. To reduce Scope 1 emissions, we have invested in the replacement of coolers, lights, and oil and gas burners with equipment that emits less CO2e. During 2023-24 we have worked with our suppliers of beverages, who own and operate beverage coolers at our stations and replaced 45 coolers, resulting in a saving of 14 tonnes of CO2e. Since 2020 we have been replacing internal combustion engine (ICE) company cars with electric and hybrid vehicles, contributing to the reduction of Scope 1 emissions. Scope 2 involves CO2e emissions generated by the electricity, heating, and cooling we purchase from suppliers for use at our own facilities. To reduce emissions in Scope 2 we purchase renewable energy and install solar panels at our service stations.

content_text: The wastewater generated during car washing contains harmful substances such as oils, heavy metals, asphalt, tire residue, and chemicals from car care products, posing a threat to local ecosystems. OKQ8 Scandinavia acknowledges the sizable water consumption in our car wash operations and its impact on local water availability. Due to our awareness of the impact of our car wash services on ecosystems, we have set the goal to recirculate water at all automatic car washes in Sweden and Denmark by 2030. There are different water treatment methods for recirculation at automatic car washes, which gives different potential reductions of water usage and pollution, the most effective showing a potential water consumption reduction of 90 percent. To identify the optimal water treatment option for OKQ8 in Sweden and Q8 in Denmark that is both cost effective and has the biggest positive effect on the environment, we are testing various options, including for example probiotic chemical water treatment. Furthermore, we have collaborated with master's degree students from Kungliga Tekniska Högskolan in Stockholm to benchmark different water treatment methods in our car wash service. Read more about this in the chapter Stakeholders. In 2023-2024 OKQ8 Scandinavia has built three new automatic car washes with biological water treatment. The plan for 2024-2025 includes the construction of three brand new car washes with biological water treatment at OKQ8, in addition to improving eight existing car washes so that they also include biological treatment of water: four each at both OKQ8 and Q8. Lastly, OKQ8 educates our Swedish customers and members through various channels about the negative environmental impact of washing cars at home. The purpose is to nudge everyone to utilize car wash facilities at service stations instead, as they are designed to reduce water usage and pollution.

content_text: The board bears responsibility for sustainability progress and performance. Operational responsibility is delegated to the Executive Management Team (EMT), which reports back to the board on a quarterly basis. The board and the CEO are responsible for the preparation and approval of the Sustainability Report and have approved the sustainability focus and impact areas, materiality analysis, sustainability targets and policy, and Code of Conduct. The result of the sustainability work in terms of progress and efficiency, as well as changes in impact on stakeholders, are presented to the board quarterly and annually by the EMT. During 2023-2024 the board approved the decision to maintain the climate target, aiming to achieve net-zero CO2e emissions in our value chain by 2035, despite the consequences of the Swedish greenhouse gas reduction mandate. The board also oversaw the preparation for enabling reporting in compliance with the CSRD from 2025-2026. The board ensures that it is kept informed and continuously updated in order to oversee sustainability progress and performance.

The Executive Management Team (EMT) is operationally responsible for sustainability progress and performance. The CEO is responsible for the implementation of the company's Code of Conduct and Sustainability Policy. Regular EMT meetings are held to review sustainability progress and to plan ahead. Reporting to the board on sustainability progress is done annually and as needed. Material noncompliance and critical concerns are reported to the EMT as they occur. Reported concerns are investigated and corrective actions are taken when necessary. The board and the EMT update and develop their sustainability related skills on a continuous basis.

content_text: Achieving our sustainability goals requires a holistic approach that involves everyone in the company, regardless of their position. OKQ8 Scandinavia also employs a team of sustainability specialists who support divisions across both Sweden and Denmark. The People and Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) functions ensure the health, well-being and safety of all employees. People also report to the Director of Sustainability, People & Communications, while EHS reports to the Director of Supply Chain & Asset Development (SCAD). The health, well-being and safety of all our employees is of the utmost importance. OKQ8 Scandinavia operates with a Code of Conduct based on the principles of the UN Global Compact within our sphere of influence. We have committed to upholding these principles and ensure that each employee receives mandatory training in order to understand the principles of our Code of Conduct. The Corporate Compliance Officer is responsible for overseeing the establishment, implementation and updating of internal rules to ensure that employees can easily comply with the Code of Conduct. No level within OKQ8 Scandinavia is exempt from compliance with the Code of Conduct. Anti-corruption is a key component of our Code of Conduct. OKQ8 Scandinavia has a legal and ethical obligation to prevent corruption and anti-competitive behavior at any level. OKQ8 Scandinavia endeavors to comply with the Swedish Anti-Corruption Institute's Code of Business Conduct. We also have a Partner Code of Conduct that our suppliers and partners must comply with, and which forms part of every contract we sign. The Partner Code of Conduct is also based on the ten principles stipulated by the UN's Global Compact. OKQ8 Bank is also vigilant with respect to corruption and has processes in place to detect suspected cases of money laundering, in compliance with government standards and legislation.

In 2023, OKQ8 Scandinavia updated our Sustainability Policy. The policy stipulates the areas in which we can make a positive impact on cultivating a corporate culture in which our sustainability focus areas are embedded in all our operations. The potential occurrence of land contamination in previous years has been generally assessed at our service stations and at all our operating fuel depots. OKQ8 Scandinavia remediates pollution in accordance with legal requirements and in dialogue with regulatory authorities. Every year, OKQ8 Scandinavia engages an external company to conduct ground surveys at locations where ground contamination has been discovered or is suspected. The fuel depots and stations work continuously on managing the impact of contamination with regards to health, safety and the environment. The fuel depots have a well-documented safety management system to reduce the risks of chemical accidents, spills or fire. Before any major or minor operational changes, risk analyses and risk assessments are carried out at fuel depots to ensure that operations can be conducted with minimal risk of incidents. Annual maintenance plans are formulated, and inspections are carried out in accordance with established conditions, laws and internal requirements. Staff are trained and conduct drills to ensure that they are prepared for any incident. The fuel depots are equipped with preventive protection devices and equipment for handling incidents. All incidents are reported and investigated, and knowledge from incidents is shared across the business for the purpose of continuous improvement.

In the event of a spill, immediate action is taken to remove and prevent the spread of the contaminant. We classify spills depending on whether they have been released to hard surfaces, where a spill can be easily contained, or to the environment, including soil and water, where more extensive efforts are required to manage and remediate spills. During the year we experienced five spills to the environment equivalent to a total volume of 862 litres, the largest single spill being 800 litres. There were also spills on hard surfaces. OK-Q8 AB also reports in accordance with relevant parts of GRI 11: Oil and Gas Sector 2021. Key activities in OK-Q8 AB's operations that are material in relation to the Oil and Gas Sector are the transportation of oil and gas, as well as the selling of oil and gas products for the purpose of fuels and gas for retail use. The report has been reviewed by OK-Q8 AB's external auditor. OK-Q8 AB has been a signatory of the UN Global Compact since 2014 and has committed to work and take responsibility for the ten principles of the initiative concerning human rights, labour rights, the environment and anti-corruption. From 2023, our Communication on Progress report with the UN Global Compact is downloadable from unglobalcompact.org. OKQ8 Scandinavia Sustainability Report 2023-2024 covers all operations within OK-Q8 AB, including all its subsidiaries in Denmark and Sweden. The Group also conducts business via a collaboration agreement in OK Detaljhandel AB, which is owned by OK ekonomisk förening. Where OK Detaljhandel AB is not included in the sustainability report, this is explained either in text or in a footnote. Individual franchises operate service stations under the OKQ8 brand in Sweden via franchise agreements with OK-Q8 AB. This is known collectively as OKQ8 Scandinavia. OK-Q8 AB is owned jointly by OK ekonomisk förening (50 percent) and Kuwait Petroleum Europe B.V (50 percent). The sustainability report is an important component of OK-Q8 AB's dialogue with different stakeholders and its aim is to promote transparency and continuous improvement.
